skill.name: render-automation
skill.description: Automates Render service discovery, deployment triggers, deployment monitoring, and project listing through Rube MCP.
skill.summary: Run Render service and deployment workflows through the Rube MCP Render toolkit.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around MCP tool names, parameters, and examples. One low network risk is confirmed for the documented rube.app MCP endpoint, and one medium semantic finding covers third-party Render operations. No prompt injection language or covert exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Third-party MCP connection can broker Render account actions.
remediation.suggestion: Document the trust boundary and recommend least-privilege Render access before users connect Rube MCP.

remediation.issue: Deployment triggers can affect live services.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation with service name, service ID, and environment before triggering deploys.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded Rube MCP endpoint is required for setup.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the endpoint visible in setup docs and warn users to verify it before adding the MCP server.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Render connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `render`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `RENDER_LIST_SERVICES` - List all services with optional filters [Required]
- Pagination uses cursor-based approach; follow `cursor` until absent
- `clearCache`: Set `true` to clear build cache before deploying
- `serviceId` is required; resolve via LIST_SERVICES first
- `clearCache: true` forces a clean build; takes longer but resolves cache-related issues
- Use `cursor` from response for next page
- Continue until `cursor` is absent or results are empty
- Set `limit` to max (100) for fewer pagination rounds
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Poll at reasonable intervals (10-30 seconds) to avoid rate limits
- Avoid rapid polling; use 10-30 second intervals

content.user_title: Automate Render Deployments with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Render operations can require repeated lookups, deploy triggers, and status checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through Rube MCP tool sequences.
actual_capabilities: Find Render services by name, type, limit, and pagination cursor.
Trigger a Render deployment for a resolved service ID.
Monitor deployment status until it reaches a terminal state.
List Render projects with cursor-based pagination.
Explain required identifiers, status values, and common deployment pitfalls.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Render connection before use.
Does not create, update, or delete Render services.
Cannot bypass Render permissions, authentication, or API rate limits.
Tool schemas may change, so it must search tools first.

use_cases.title: Review Render Service Inventory
use_cases.description: List services by name or type and capture IDs needed for later operations.

use_cases.title: Run Controlled Redeploys
use_cases.description: Resolve the correct service, trigger a deploy, and monitor progress until completion.

use_cases.title: Check Deployment Health
use_cases.description: Retrieve deploy status and identify whether a build is live, failed, canceled, or still running.

prompt_templates.title: List Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube tools, then list my Render web services. Show service names, IDs, types, and whether more pages are available.

prompt_templates.title: Find and Deploy a Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube tools, find the Render service named api, confirm the service ID with me, then trigger a new deploy.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube tools, retrieve the latest deploy status for this service and deploy ID, and summarize progress and failure details.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Projects and Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Rube tools, list Render projects and services with pagination, then summarize project coverage and services without project assignment.

output_examples.input: List Render web services that match api.
output_examples.output: A concise inventory with matching service names, service IDs, service types, and pagination status.

output_examples.input: Redeploy the production API after I confirm the target.
output_examples.output: A deployment summary with the resolved service ID, deploy ID, cache choice, current status, and next polling step.

output_examples.input: Check whether this deployment is live or failed.
output_examples.output: A status report that names the terminal state, finish time when available, and any build or update failure signal.

best_practices: Search Rube tools before each workflow to confirm current Render schemas.
Resolve service names to service IDs before deployment actions.
Use 10-30 second polling intervals when monitoring deployments.
anti_patterns: Triggering deployments without confirming the target service and environment.
Polling deployment status rapidly after every request.
Assuming service names are unique without checking the returned results.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Render service listing, deployment triggers, deployment status checks, and project listing through Rube MCP.

faq.question: Does it require a Render connection?
faq.answer: Yes. Rube MCP must be connected, and the Render toolkit connection must be active before workflows run.

faq.question: Can it create new Render services?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows cover listing services, triggering deploys, checking deploys, and listing projects.

faq.question: Why should tools be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first confirms current parameters before a Render operation is attempted.

faq.question: How does it avoid wrong deployments?
faq.answer: It resolves service names to Render service IDs and should confirm the target before triggering a deploy.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clients that can use Rube MCP.
